note: Headcount, where it sits, and what the work actually is. Employee numbers are the most recently reported figure for each company and are not all from the same date, so each carries its own — a company that reported in March 2026 is not being compared like-for-like with one that reported in December 2025.

outlook.note: US pharmaceutical manufacturing, projected by the Bureau of Labor Statistics — about 5% growth, and close to 19,000 added production jobs, which ranks it among the faster-growing industries it tracks.

roles.title: Field application scientist
roles.what: Installs the instrument and teaches the lab to use it
roles.wants: A science degree and the willingness to travel

roles.title: R&D engineer
roles.what: Builds the optics, fluidics and software inside the machine

roles.title: Technical support scientist
roles.what: Works out why someone's assay stopped working

roles.title: Process development scientist
roles.what: Gets a cell line to make more protein, more consistently

roles.title: QC analyst
roles.what: Tests each batch against specification before it ships
roles.wants: A science degree; GMP training on the job

roles.title: Supply chain planner
roles.what: Keeps a factory from running out of a resin with a nine-month lead time

roles.title: Computational chemist
roles.what: Predicts which molecules are worth making before anyone makes them

roles.title: Machine learning engineer
roles.what: Trains models on assay and structure data
roles.wants: ML; biology picked up on the job

roles.title: Scientific software engineer
roles.what: Builds the tools the scientists actually use

roles.title: Toxicologist
roles.what: Finds the dose at which the drug does harm, before a person takes it

roles.title: Study director
roles.what: Owns one safety study end to end and signs the report
roles.wants: Years in the lab, then accountability

roles.title: Bioanalytical chemist
roles.what: Measures how much drug is in a sample, at very low concentrations

roles.title: Veterinary technician
roles.what: Cares for the animals and runs the dosing

roles.title: Process engineer
roles.what: Scales a recipe from a flask to a two-thousand-litre bioreactor

roles.title: Validation engineer
roles.what: Proves to a regulator that the equipment does what is claimed
roles.wants: Engineering and a tolerance for documentation

roles.title: QA specialist
roles.what: Reviews the batch record and decides whether it can be released
roles.wants: A science degree and GMP experience

roles.title: Aseptic operator
roles.what: Fills sterile vials without contaminating them
roles.wants: Trained in-house; the bar is discipline

roles.title: Clinical research associate
roles.what: Visits the hospitals running the trial and checks the data against the source records
roles.wants: A life-science degree; the classic way in

roles.title: Clinical data manager
roles.what: Builds the database and chases every discrepancy in it
roles.wants: Data skills; the science can follow

roles.title: Biostatistician
roles.what: Writes the analysis plan and decides what the result means
roles.wants: A master's in statistics or biostatistics

roles.title: Epidemiologist
roles.what: Designs the study and works out who to compare with whom
roles.wants: A master's or doctorate in epidemiology

roles.title: Medical writer
roles.what: Turns the analysis into the protocol, the report and the filing
roles.wants: Scientific training and the ability to write

roles.title: Pharmacovigilance associate
roles.what: Records and reports every adverse event, for the life of the drug

roles.title: Regulatory affairs associate
roles.what: Assembles the submission and answers the agency's questions

roles.title: Medicinal chemist
roles.what: Designs and makes the molecules
roles.wants: A doctorate in organic chemistry, usually

roles.title: In-vivo pharmacologist
roles.what: Tests whether the molecule does anything in an animal model

roles.title: Translational scientist
roles.what: Decides which patients the drug should be tried in first
roles.wants: A doctorate, and often a clinical background

roles.title: Medical science liaison
roles.what: Explains the evidence to specialists who prescribe

roles.title: HEOR analyst
roles.what: Builds the case that the drug is worth what it costs
roles.wants: Health economics, epidemiology or public health

roles.title: Market access manager
roles.what: Negotiates with the people who decide whether it is paid for

roles.title: Drug safety physician
roles.what: Judges whether a reported harm was caused by the drug

roles.title: Pharmacist
roles.what: The last check before the drug reaches a person
roles.wants: A pharmacy degree and a licence

roles.title: Cold chain specialist
roles.what: Keeps a biologic within two degrees of where it must stay, across an ocean

pay.basis: US median annual wage, all industries, from the Bureau of Labor Statistics. These are the national median for the occupation everywhere it is practised, not a pharma-only number — pharmaceutical employers generally pay above them, so read them as a floor and a ranking rather than an offer.

occupations.title: Medical & health services managers
occupations.note: Runs a site, a programme or a department

occupations.title: Pharmacists
occupations.note: Dispenses, and increasingly reviews the therapy

occupations.title: Chemical engineers
occupations.note: Scales a reaction from flask to reactor

occupations.title: Statisticians
occupations.note: Designs the trial and reads out the endpoint

occupations.title: Epidemiologists
occupations.note: Tracks who the disease hits and how hard

occupations.title: Biological technicians
occupations.note: Runs the bench work the rest of it depends on

sources: Company headcounts: most recently reported figures as compiled in 2026 industry surveys of the largest pharmaceutical employers, and company reporting. Dates differ by company and are shown per row.
Europe: EFPIA, 'The Pharmaceutical Industry in Figures' — direct employment across member countries, around 950,000, with the national figures shown from the same dataset.
United States: brand-name pharmaceutical manufacturing 352,022 and generic 39,569 as of 2026 (IBISWorld industry employment series).
Outlook: US Bureau of Labor Statistics employment projections, 2024–34, for pharmaceutical and medicine manufacturing.
Roles are the ones each stage routinely advertises for and what those jobs involve. They are descriptive, not a count of open positions — no vacancy figures are claimed here.

Pay: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Outlook Handbook — median annual wage by occupation, all industries (May 2025; biological technicians May 2024). Not pharma-specific: the industry generally pays above these medians.
